evidence: fetchRepos now names the 100-item page size once and uses it for both query construction and pagination termination.

findings.summary: Repository eligibility and case-insensitive de-duplication are implemented twice in the project loader, once when a fetched page is appended and again in the stale-cache preview callback, so the two paths must be kept identical by hand.

assessment.reason: The preview must show exactly the cards a successful refresh would append, so a change to the eligibility or name-matching rule has to be made in two places in the most intricate loading flow. One shared helper keeps the live and preview results from drifting.
evidence: assets/script.js:185-201: fetchNextProjects applies eligibleProjects and lowercase-name matching against seenProjects, adding each accepted name to it.
assets/script.js:233-245: the loadMoreProjects stale callback repeats the same eligibility and lowercase-name filter against a copied Set to build previewProjects.

test/script.test.cjs: shows expired data immediately then replaces it, replaces a failed cached later-page preview while preserving earlier cards, and does not repeat cards when repositories move between API pages exercise both paths.
assessment.invariant: Keep repository eligibility, case-insensitive name matching and API order identical in the live and preview paths. A preview must still leave seenProjects and pagination untouched until a live page succeeds, and the rendered cards, status text and retry behavior must not change.

evidence: assets/script.js now defines newProjects(repos, seen) once; fetchNextProjects calls it with seenProjects and the stale-preview callback calls it with new Set(seenProjects), so eligibility and lowercase-name matching exist in one place.

findings.summary: loadMoreProjects picks the post-load focus target with a nested ternary inside its finally block, mixing state reset, aria updates and focus choice in one place.

assessment.reason: The focus rules (first new card, existing last card, final count, or none) are accessibility behavior that the next maintainer must decode from a three-level ternary before changing anything. findings.summary: loadProjectRelease and loadProjectLicense repeat the same cached-request, render and ignore-failure flow, differing only in endpoint, validator and renderer.

assessment.reason: The shared contract (use the five-minute cache, render stale data while refreshing, never interrupt browsing on failure) lives in two copies, so a change to it needs two coordinated edits. One small helper keeps the knowledge in one place.
evidence: assets/script.js:480-503: both functions call cachedGitHub with a render callback, render the response and swallow errors in a catch block

test/script.test.cjs: caches release responses, refreshes expired versions and retains them after a failed refresh; caches licenses, preserves a focused link during refresh and keeps stale data after failure; hides failed or unsafe license results; omits missing, unavailable, unsafe, blank, draft or prerelease versions cover both flows
assessment.invariant: Keep the request URLs, validators, cache keys, license-only-when-advertised rule, stale-then-fresh rendering, quiet failure and the existing function names used by retry callbacks unchanged.
